title: Third-party SDK traffic on the watchlist
intro: In 60 s on the idle watchlist the app contacted 9 third-party domains (Plotline, VWO, Google Firebase, CleverTap, MoEngage, Protectt.ai, AppsFlyer). Most of these SDKs are started for the whole app, not by this module, so the main item is a Product and BE decision. The watchlist itself mounts a Plotline banner and a Plotline-tracked kebab on every open, which is worth checking.

measured.metric: Third-party domains contacted in 60 s on the screen (X3)
measured.expected: depends on I1; ≈ 5–6 if analytics SDKs batch and VWO/Plotline stop polling on this screen (to be confirmed with PCAPdroid)
slightly lower if I1 removes idle SDK polling

changes.title: Decide which SDKs may use the network on the watchlist
changes.summary: Ask Product and BE which of the SDKs seen on the idle watchlist (Plotline, VWO, Firebase, CleverTap, MoEngage, Protectt.ai, AppsFlyer) must talk to the network there, and whether batching/flush intervals can be raised.
changes.risk_reason: A decision and SDK configuration review; no code in this plan.
changes.product_decision: Which SDKs are required while a user sits on the watchlist? Can analytics flush every 60 s or on background instead of immediately? Is VWO needed on this screen?
changes.be_request: Share each SDK's flush/poll configuration (CleverTap, MoEngage, AppsFlyer, VWO, Plotline, Protectt.ai) and whether it can be changed from the dashboard.
changes.current: X3 counted 9 domains first seen within the 60 s capture while the app was idle on Bench 20. The SDKs are initialised at app level (apps/super_app); this plan did not analyse their initialisation line by line.
steps: Collect each SDK's network behaviour with PCAPdroid per SDK domain.
Product decides; BE/marketing change dashboard settings where possible.
regression_checks: Analytics dashboards still receive events after any configuration change.
changes.after_improvement: Fewer third-party connections from the idle watchlist; exact count after the decision.

changes.title: Check what the Plotline widgets do on each open
changes.summary: The watchlist mounts PlotlineWidget(watchlistBannerKey) above the list on every open and wraps the kebab in a Plotline PView. Check with the Plotline SDK whether these widgets fetch or report on mount when no campaign targets them, and render them only when a campaign is active if they do.
changes.risk_reason: Investigation first; any change keeps the widgets when a campaign is configured.
changes.product_decision: May the watchlist banner slot be skipped when no Plotline campaign targets it?

files.change: Investigate; if needed, build PlotlineWidget only when a campaign exists for the key.
Investigate the PView wrapper on the kebab.

changes.current: When the header part of the body builds for WatchlistLoaded, it inserts const PlotlineWidget(valueKey: PlotLineWidgetKey.watchlistBannerKey). The kebab menu is wrapped in PView(valueKey: PlotlineCampaignEvent.kebabMenuInWatchlistEvent). Plotline is one of the 9 third-party domains seen in X3. Whether these widgets cause network calls is not visible from this repo (SDK code) (verify with PCAPdroid filtered to Plotline's domain while opening the tab).
steps: Open/close the tab 10 times with PCAPdroid filtered to Plotline; count requests.
If requests scale with opens, ask Plotline for a campaign-presence check and gate the widget.
safety: Campaigns keep working; only an empty slot is skipped.
regression_checks: A test campaign on the watchlist banner still shows.
changes.after_improvement: Fewer Plotline requests per watchlist open, if the check confirms them.
